platforms.name: Architect + Lyzr Agent Studio
platforms.position: Best reference in this study for combining application generation with an explicit agent platform.
platforms.access: App build and revision exercised. Studio onboarding, agent configuration, API deployment surface and a saved workflow template explored. App publishing and real external actions were not executed.
journey: Start
Open organization home; choose prompt, library, theme or Import codebase.
Observed: project lists, prompt options, 58 design presets and public/private repository entry paths.
Novices can begin with intent; importing must remain a separate first-class entry.
Plan
Submit common brief; answer planning clarification with the standard response.
Exercised: Lyzr-agent vs GitAgent choice, editable PRD and mockup artifacts.
The user has to understand the relationship between agents, plan and mockup.
Build
Choose Start building, select plan and mockup, then Build with these.
Exercised: streamed actions, delegation, token use and commit/revert affordances.
Multiple approvals offer control but repeat the transition from planning to execution.
Preview and recover
Open App preview; use Reload preview after the error.
Exercised: usable preview recovered; Console and more actions available.
Recovery should describe what failed and preserve the last usable preview.
Edit and inspect
Send revision in chat; open More actions and View File Tree.
Exercised chat revision; inspected 123-file tree, download, duplication, environment and test controls.
File visibility is useful; direct file editing was not verified.
Configure agents
Open Agents → Edit Agents in Studio; complete separate Studio login.
Exercised transition; inspected Build / Playground / Deploy, models, instructions, tools and output formats.
Architect agent panel was empty while Studio contained a generated backbone agent: context continuity needs attention.
Orchestrate
Studio → Orchestrate → SuperFlow → template → saved support approval workflow.
Exercised creation and node inspection. Run opens input panel; actual workflow execution not tested.
Canvas supports branching, approval and code, but brings considerable technical vocabulary.
Ship
Open Deploy; inspect marketplace, hosting and GitHub ownership choices.
Observed setup only: metadata, custom domain, default Lyzr private GitHub or connect own account.
Publish to Marketplace defaulted on; visitor credit consumption appeared in setup. Visibility and cost need explicit review.
features: Organizations; My/Published/Shared projects; prompt attachments; Studio agents; themes; prompt library; consultant/idea discovery; usage filters.
Observed; consultant form and marketplace result not fully completed.
Plan / Agents / App; editable PRD and mockup; build trace; console; token count; commit; revert; preview reload.
Build and recovery exercised; revert not executed.
Feature testing toggle; clear chat/agents; download code; environment variables beta; duplicate; file tree; delete.
Menu and file tree inspected. Destructive controls not activated.
Public repo URL / private GitHub import entry; own GitHub connection; default managed repo; domains; app metadata; marketplace publishing.
Setup inspected; import, OAuth grant and final publish not completed.
Registry; role / goal / instructions; Generate / Improve; manager agents; A2A; provider/model picker; comparison; routing; parameters; knowledge; tools; skills; schedule/trigger.
Editor controls inspected; existing backbone agent not modified.
Sessions; chat and attachments; Activity / Artifacts; version history; Text examples; JSON schema; image and document formats.
Surfaces inspected; format settings not enabled.
Data Query; Memory; Context; Voice; Responsible AI; fairness/bias; reflection; groundedness; LLM-as-judge beta.
Available controls inspected; several advanced controls displayed upgrade gates.
API instructions and masked credential; cURL; A2A agent card/discovery/execution; Agent JSON; App Store publishing.
Inspected; credentials not revealed; no external invocation or publishing.

Agent, A2A, Swarm, Tool, LLM, Decide, Rank; Guardrails; Trigger, If, Switch, Merge, Filter, Loop, Wait, Approval, Stop/Error, No-Op; Set, Aggregate, Sort, Limit, Deduplicate, Rename, TOON; Code, HTTP, nested SuperFlow; Date/Time, Crypto; document parse/extract/label.
Palette observed; GitAgent and Split Document marked soon. Only template creation/node configuration inspected.
Templates; import; undo/redo; align/expand; save; execution history; approvals; JSON export; run panel; zoom; minimap; structured outputs; model parameters.
Saved template and opened run input. History, import/export and approvals listed but not executed end to end.
Knowledge Base, Knowledge Graph, Semantic Model, Skills, Global Context; Traces, Transcripts, Reports; Models, Voice Providers, Tools, Data Connectors, Memory, Guardrails, Telephony.
Navigation inventory captured; downstream configuration not completed.
Responsible AI, Simulation Engine, Improvement Engine; Voice; Blueprints; App Store; search; help; credits.
Safety entries gated by upgrade; discovery/navigation inspected.
good: Explicit plan artifacts before generation make a complex build reviewable.
The Studio offers a rich agent lifecycle beyond a generic chat-to-website builder.
Recovery, code download and ownership choices are discoverable in the project context.
friction: A separate Studio login and context switch interrupt the app-to-agent journey.
The empty Architect agent panel did not explain the existing Studio backbone agent.
Deployment combines marketplace visibility, hosting and credit consequences; defaults need clearer explanation.
platforms.lesson: Keep one project context across Plan, Preview, Code, Agents and Deploy. Offer plain-language defaults with advanced configuration on demand.

Security panel inspected; deep scan not run; growth tools only inventoried.
Name/subdomain, owner, counters, category, live preview, analytics/AI context/autofix controls, badge, trust center, sharing, remix/cross-project context, transfer, unpublish/delete.

market.methodology: Internet research snapshot: 26 September 2026. Figures are the specific public claims located in this review, not audited current totals. Publication date and retrieval date are different. Undated pages are marked explicitly. Prefer company publications and documentation; press and partner claims are identified. People can use several products, so do not sum these numbers or calculate market share. No like-for-like popularity leaderboard is justified by these data.
market.interpretation: Positioning is the vendor’s product promise, paraphrased. Differentiation is our synthesis, not an exclusive-capability claim. Reasons for use are supported by product descriptions, selected customer stories or company usage research; inference is labeled. These sources do not replace interviews with users or a representative satisfaction survey.

design_implications: Start from the user’s job: create a new app, automate a workflow, or continue an existing repository. These intents need different entry points into the same project.
Make the first useful outcome easy for a non-technical builder, then progressively expose code, agent logic, integrations and deployment controls.
Give Architect a clear promise around agentic applications: make it easy to understand what each agent does and how the app uses it.
Connect the prototype to ownership and ongoing operation: editing, debugging, testing, GitHub, deployment and monitoring should form a continuous journey.
Use adoption figures as market context. Choose product priorities from user needs and the hands-on evidence, not the largest incomparable number.
